entries.name: Minnesota Hmong New Year
entries.capsule: Two days at Saint Paul RiverCentre each late fall: dance and singing contests, pageant, ball toss, food and family.
entries.dateRule: Set each year by The United Hmong Family, Inc. Recent years fell on the weekend after Thanksgiving. Home rituals are separate from the public event, and other towns hold their own dates.

dates.source: Saint Paul RiverCentre; The United Hmong Family

entries.whatItMarks: The end of the harvest and of the old year. Noj Peb Caug translates to "eat 30." The public opening includes a symbolic sweeping away of the old year's misfortunes, and families make offerings to ancestors and may hold soul-calling at home.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: At RiverCentre, 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. both days, with a ribbon cutting Saturday morning, a grand opening show at Roy Wilkins Auditorium, dance and singing competitions, the Hmong Minnesota Pageant, ball toss, food and vendors. The 2025 event was the 45th, drawing more than 26,000 by RiverCentre's count; the organizer cited over 31,000 in Senate testimony for an earlier year. Adult tickets for 2026 are about $15 to $17.51; seniors 65 and over and children under 42 inches are free.

entries.name: Hmong Special Guerrilla Units Remembrance Day
alsoKnownAs: Hmong-Lao Veterans Memorial Day (name in 2019 House release)
entries.capsule: Minnesota's day, set in state law, to honor Hmong who served in the Secret War in Laos, 1961 to 1975.
entries.dateRule: May 14 each year, by Minnesota statute. If it falls on a weekend, schools are encouraged to mark it the Friday before.
entries.whatItMarks: May 14, 1975, when the American-trained Hmong command structure ceased operating. It honors those who served in the Secret War. General Vang Pao's departure from Laos, as named in the seed entry, is the same event in many accounts, but the statute frames the day around the Special Guerrilla Units.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: By law the governor issues a proclamation and orders flags at half-staff on Capitol grounds; schools are encouraged to teach Hmong history. St. Paul Public Schools suggests books, traditional clothing, displays and music for Hmong American Day. Its 2019 sponsor, Rep. Tou Xiong, hoped schools would use the day to teach the war. A 2026 bill for a Hmong Heritage Week, May 14 to 20, was at the introduction stage when checked.
entries.workplaceNote: Minn. Stat. 10.5805 says businesses may close in honor of this day and an employee may request the day off in observance. It does not make the day a paid or required holiday in the wording checked.

entries.name: Hmong International Freedom Festival
entries.capsule: Two summer days at Como Park's McMurray Field: kato, soccer, food, vendors and family reunions from across the country.
entries.dateRule: Set each year by The United Hmong Family. Long tied to the Fourth of July weekend; held on the last weekend of June in 2024, 2025 and 2026.

dates.source: Visit Saint Paul; KARE 11 confirms the event was held

entries.whatItMarks: Reconnecting Hmong people separated by war, and Hmong freedom in the United States. The 2026 event was billed as the 44th, marking 50 years of Hmong freedom in Minnesota.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: McMurray Field, 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. both days, $10 in 2026, with kato or sepak takraw, soccer, volleyball, flag football, tuj lub, vendors and music. Reported attendance ranges from 35,507 in 2023, from a University of Minnesota Extension survey as reported by Hoodline, to about 57,000 in 2024 per the organizer. Sources date its start to the 1970s or 1980. Lao Family Community of Minnesota ran it in 2013; The United Hmong Family runs it now.

entries.name: Hmong Minnesota Day at the State Fair
entries.capsule: Labor Day at the Minnesota State Fair: Hmong singers, dancers, martial artists and community leaders on stage.
entries.dateRule: On Labor Day, the last day of the Minnesota State Fair, in past years. The fair confirms each year's schedule; Labor Day in 2027 falls on Sept. 6, and in 2028 on Sept. 4.

dates.source: The fair says the page is not yet updated for 2027; projected Sept. 6 if the Labor Day pattern holds

entries.whatItMarks: Hmong achievement in Minnesota. It began in 2015, marking four decades. The 2024 event honored founder Tou Ger Xiong.
